one_line: A 9-second single-shot close-up of a baby's face (tongue visible) under one text card, 'Forget crawling...this is a milestone they never tell you about', with a long expert-style caption about tongue clicking and oral-motor development.

hook.visual: Tight close-up of a smiling baby in a green top, head turned slightly to the side, looking off camera, mouth open with the tongue visible.
hook.on_screen_text: Forget crawling...this is a milestone they never tell you about (followed by a teary-smile emoji and a speaker emoji) (English on screen, no translation needed)
hook.first_spoken_line: That is so cool. (Whisper only, low reliability: one line spread across 0 to 7.4 s)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: A baby's face fills the whole frame from frame one, and the text dismisses a famous milestone (crawling) in favour of a secret one, which opens a curiosity gap. The speaker emoji signals that the sound is the point.

beats.observed: Close-up of the baby, head turned to the left, smiling with the lips slightly parted, eyes looking off camera. White text card sits over the baby's chest from the first frame.
beats.spoken: Whisper: 'That is so cool.' (unverified, may be a parent off camera or a hallucination).
beats.on_screen_text: Forget crawling...this is a milestone they never tell you about

beats.observed: Baby leans toward the camera; at 3.0 s mouth is wide open with the tongue raised, at 4.0 s lips close in a closed-mouth smile.
Repeated small mouth and tongue movements: mouth parted at 5.0 s, tongue visible inside the open mouth at 6.0 s, wide smile at 7.0 s. The baby keeps glancing off camera.
Mouth open at 8.0 s; at 9.0 s the tongue is pushed out between the lips. Video ends on this expression.

payoff: There is no single reveal: the viewer gets the baby's tongue behaviour continuously from 0 to 9 s. The tongue is stuck out at 9.0 s. The audible click the caption talks about cannot be confirmed from frames or transcript.
cta: none. The caption closes with 'Give your child time, watch with curiosity, and let them experiment', which is advice, not an ask.
share_or_comment_trigger: 'My baby does that too' recognition. Shares (178) are 0.59 per like, much higher than the 0.02 per like on the SHOW video in this batch, so parents appear to be sending it to a partner or friend.
why_it_worked: 13.1x the account median of 1,168 views (15,300 views) with a 1.99% like rate: an organic pattern.
178 shares on 304 likes: highly sendable 'look, ours does this' content, driven by one familiar baby behaviour.
9 seconds, one shot, one text card: short enough that most viewers likely loop or finish it (inferred, no watch-time data), and the sound-on emoji makes the clip feel like it needs the audio.
paid_signal: no, like rate is 1.99%, well above the 0.3% level that would suggest paid promotion.

solo_route.how: 1) Collect a short clip of a baby doing a charming early behaviour (tongue sounds, raspberries, first laugh) from LumeBook's creator or UGC pool, or ask parents who already tag the brand, and get written permission to post it with credit. 2) In CapCut or Canva trim to 8 to 10 s, keep the original audio, and add one white text card in the lower third: 'Forget X...this is a milestone they never tell you about' plus a speaker emoji. 3) Put the educational explanation in the caption, have a barter expert check it, and open the cited paper yourself: the caption here cites a study titled 'Premature Infant Swallowing...', which is about premature infants, so check that any source you cite actually supports your sentence.
solo_route.needs: Written permission from the baby's parent, and ideally a barter expert to vet the caption. Do not use AI-generated baby footage for a 'milestone' claim, because the point is a real baby.

lumebook_version.hook_he: שכחו זחילה, זאת אבן הדרך שאף אחד לא מספר לכם עליה
lumebook_version.concept: An 8 to 10 s permissioned parent clip of a baby doing a quirky first, with one white text card and a sound-on emoji. The caption explains the milestone with a verified source and ends with a soft line pointing to a LumeBook milestones book.

evidence_notes: Observed: baby face, the single text card present in every frame, tongue and mouth positions at 3, 6 and 9 s. Spoken: Whisper gives one line, 'That is so cool.', spread over 0 to 7.44 s; this is low reliability and I cannot tell who says it. I cannot hear the tongue click, so the caption's claim that the baby is clicking is NOT visibly proven by the frames, only consistent with the tongue movement. All developmental claims (oral-motor coordination, feeding, speech) come from the caption only. The cited Goldfield et al. title in the caption refers to premature infant swallowing, which I note as a possible weak fit for the claim (my inference, not verified). Who filmed the clip is not stated.
